extracted.intended_audience: prospective IFAD regular grants applicants (developing Member States, UN agencies, civil society organisations, research/academic institutions, producer organisations, foundations, private companies)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility rules for applying to IFAD's regular grants programme, which funds country, regional, or global activities that support inclusive rural transformation and SDG objectives. Intended for organisations legally constituted in IFAD Member States seeking non‑repayable grant funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipient legal constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible recipients must have been legally constituted in an IFAD Member State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict eligibility requirement for receiving IFAD regular grants; applicants must demonstrate legal constitution in an IFAD Member State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of eligible recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of IFAD grants include developing Member States, intergovernmental organizations (including United Nations agencies), civil society organizations, research and academic institutions, producer organizations, foundations and private companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The programme accepts a broad range of entity types; prospective applicants should confirm their organisational type matches one of the listed eligible categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and thematic alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD’s regular grants programme supports inclusive rural transformation and helps achieve the Sustainable Development Goals by leveraging our impact on the ground, including by building capacity, and fostering a more conducive policy and investment environment for smallholder agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly align with inclusive rural transformation, capacity building, improving policy/investment environments, and contributions to SDG targets and smallholder agriculture outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope / grant type
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular grants fund activities in a single country (country-specific grants) or in several countries (global and regional grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must identify whether the proposed activity is country-specific, regional, or global and ensure the proposal fits the stated geographic scope for the chosen grant type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑repayable financing
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular grants do not need to be repaid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding provided under this programme is grant financing (non‑repayable); applicants should plan budgets accordingly and not expect loan terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementarity with IFAD operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities funded through regular grants are integral to IFAD’s work and complement other development instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate how the activity is integral to IFAD’s mandate and how it complements (rather than duplicates) other IFAD-funded programmes or development instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with IFAD policies and financing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are provided in accordance with IFAD Regular Grants Policy and the Financing Procedures for IFAD Regular Grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the IFAD Regular Grants Policy, Financing Procedures, and use required grant forms; proposals will be assessed and administered according to those formal documents.
